nodes.question: How is nuclear energy positioned in the context of Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030?
nodes.answer: Nuclear energy is emphasized as a strategic development to diversify the energy portfolio, enhance energy security, and establish Saudi Arabia as a leader in innovative energy technologies.
nodes.paragraph: Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering (2025) 50:2945 https://doi.org/10.1007/s13369-25-10023-1 EDITORIAL Concluding Preface Afaque Shams1 Khaled Al-Athel1 Iztok Tiselj2 Bojan Ni ceno3 Ihsan ulhaq Toor1 Published online: 20 February 2025 King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals 2025 The rapidly evolving energy landscape demands sustainable, ef cient, and environmentally responsible solutions to meet the growing global energy needs. Nuclear energy, with itspotential to provide reliable and clean energy, remains acornerstone of this transformation. This is particularly sig- ni cant for Saudi Arabia, where Vision 2030 emphasizes the strategic development of nuclear energy to diversify itsenergy portfolio, enhance energy security, and establish the Kingdom as a leader in innovative energy technologies. This special issue, Challenges and Recent Advancements in Nuclear Energy Systems has brought together an array of studies, insights, and innovations that address critical aspects of the growth of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes. Itserves as a comprehensive resource, covering a wide range oftopics essential for advancing nuclear energy systems, with a particular focus on their relevance to Saudi Arabia S nuclear ambitions. Key contributions in this issue explore Saudi Arabia S nuclear initiatives, offering an overview of the Kingdom S roadmap toward becoming the Middle East S largest producerof nuclear energy.

nodes.question: What is the augmented Formation MCDM perspective for identifying the optimal location of renewable energy power plants?
nodes.answer: The augmented Formation MCDM perspective combines multiple criteria decision-making methods with Formation logic to identify the optimal location of renewable energy power plants based on a comprehensive set of factors and preferences.

nodes.question: What is the primary energy source that was deployed under the REFIT scheme in Ireland?
nodes.answer: The primary energy source deployed under the REFIT scheme in Ireland was wind energy.
nodes.paragraph: 3In some cases, renewables can receive a xed price support independent of wholesale market prices (for a discussion, see Alolo et al. 2020 ). Often, the policy cost is in uenced by the wholesale market price. The Irish system presents a good example of this. Renewable energy generation, predominantly wind, deployedfrom approximately 2006 to 2015 was supported under the Renewable Energy Feed-in Tariff (REFIT) scheme(Government of Ireland 2020a ). This was a guaranteed price, similar to policies in place in many markets (for a discussion, see Alolo et al. 2020 and the policy cost was the difference between the market price and the pre-agreed strike price (Farrell et al. 2017 ). Under this scheme, generators retain all remuneration should the market price exceed the strike price. Since closure of the REFIT scheme, Irish renewable energyis supported by the Renewable Energy Support Scheme (RESS) (Government of Ireland 2020b ). This is a contracts for differences-style price support, with similar schemes in place in the other jurisdictions such asthe UK (Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy 2022 ; Department for Environment, Climate and Communications 2023 ).
